RIVERBEND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT

123 Harbor Ave, Millbrook, NH 03055 Tel 555-0177

TRIAGE / NURSING NOTE

PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE
Priya Reyes	05/22/1990	771-4402-R	03/02/2024

CHIEF COMPLAINT: Neck and lower back pain following a motor vehicle collision.

HPI: Patient states she was stopped at a red light on 03/01/2024 at approximately 5:40 PM when her vehicle was struck from behind by another car. She did not lose consciousness. She drove herself home and the pain worsened overnight, prompting this ED visit the following morning.

VITALS: BP 128/82, HR 88, RR 16, Temp 98.4F, SpO2 99% RA

Pain (0-10): 7 at triage

Allergies: NKDA

Triage acuity: 3 (urgent)

RIVERBEND EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT

ED PHYSICIAN NOTE

PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE
Priya Reyes	05/22/1990	771-4402-R	03/02/2024

HISTORY: 33-year-old female, restrained driver, low-speed rear-end collision 03/01/2024. Denies head strike, denies loss of consciousness, denies numbness or tingling in extremities.

EXAM: Cervical spine - tenderness to palpation over paraspinal muscles C4-C6, no step-off, range of motion limited by pain. Lumbar spine - tenderness over bilateral paraspinal muscles L4-S1, no midline tenderness. Neurologic exam grossly intact, 5/5 strength all extremities, normal sensation.

IMAGING: Cervical spine and lumbar spine X-rays obtained, reviewed by me. No fracture, no subluxation, no acute bony abnormality identified.

ASSESSMENT: Acute cervical strain. Acute lumbar strain. Motor vehicle collision, low-speed, rear impact.

PLAN: Ibuprofen 600mg PO TID with food. Cyclobenzaprine 5mg PO at bedtime PRN muscle spasm. Ice/heat alternating. Follow up with orthopedics within 1 week if not improving. Return precautions given.

Dr. Wendell Marsh, MD - Emergency Medicine
NPI 1938204471 - Signed 03/02/2024

PATIENT	DOB	MRN	DATE OF SERVICE

WORK STATUS: Patient excused from work duties from 03/02/2024 through 03/05/2024 (3 days). May return to light duty thereafter as tolerated.

FOLLOW-UP: Orthopedic follow-up recommended within 7 days for persistent symptoms.

Discharge condition: Stable, ambulatory.

Dr. Wendell Marsh, MD - Emergency Medicine
